trust_decision.summary: Users with subscribers:sql_query may inject an arbitrary SQL WHERE expression; core decides whether the resulting statement touches only allow-listed tables by walking its EXPLAIN plan (validateQueryTables) before running it.

landing_point.why: Summary names /api/subscribers/export; the handler cmd/subscribers.go:149 calls core ExportSubscribers, which splices the expression into query-subscribers-for-export at internal/core/subscribers.go:249.

fix_sites.entry_point: internal helper reached from both routes above

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All published source changes sit in internal/core/subscribers.go; the second commit (ef0a758, internal/migrations/v6.2.0.go) is an unrelated migration idempotency change.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The by-query routes are write-only bulk actions (delete/blocklist/list management) that return no rows, need subscribers:manage as well as sql_query, and the advisory names only the export route, so a solver can argue there is no read-out channel and they are out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate sql_query expressions using allow-listed tables (subscriber_lists, campaign_views, link_clicks, bounces subqueries, attribs JSON operators) must keep working; an over-broad fix (rejecting subqueries/keywords, or a mistyped allow-list as the pre-fix 'subscribers_lists' entry) breaks the advanced-query UI on list, export and bulk-by-query.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Shared compileSubscriberQueryTpl dry-run is the only gate for all by-query routes; it checks read-only, not table access
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Lower-level models package; comment frames its purpose as a read-only check only

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Move the table allow-list check into ExecSubQueryTpl for some templates but not others (e.g. delete but not list-management).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The dry run already exists here as the one gate, so a maintainer could plausibly add the check in one place and miss the others.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: How-type: the plan walker collects only 'Relation Name' nodes, so table access that never shows up as a plan relation (e.g. SQL-executing built-in functions) is never seen.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Plan-based allow-listing is a real design choice here; an engineer must understand what EXPLAIN does and does not show.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: getSubscriberCount builds its own count statement from the same expression; a copy that validates a different template than the one it runs would be realistic.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Count and fetch templates are kept as separate replicas (queries/subscribers.sql:300-312).
